answer: Each agent identity requires a 300-unit bond locked against one hardware credential, giving the registry a costly anchor to verify a forge. A sybil attacker locking N identities must fund 300×N units upfront and forfeits 100 percent on challenge after a 14-epoch wait. Splitting identities multiplies that marginal cost, and independent jurors tracing shared bond owners can strip the haven a copied credential would otherwise buy, leaving no pearl of profit.
